claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few questions:

First, do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

Next question: Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to ask:

Do you make regular financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or towards his accommodation)? And if so, how much do you contribute?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute about £10 a week towards his needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

Just to clarify - do you know who Alex currently lives with? Is it another parent, a relative, or someone else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum, my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. 

One more important question: Do you know if Alex's mum is currently claiming Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure whether she's claiming it or not to be honest.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about that.

Let me explain the situation based on the information you've provided:

According to the Child Benefit rules, only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child. You would normally qualify if you're responsible for Alex, which typically means either:
- Living with him, OR
- Paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards his upkeep

The current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child. You mentioned you contribute about £10 per week, which is less than this amount.

Since Alex lives with his mum and you're contributing £10 per week (which is less than the Child Benefit amount), and you don't know if his mum is claiming, here's what this means:

- If his mum is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex, she would continue to receive it as only one person can claim per child
- Even if she's not claiming, your current contribution level (£10/week) is below the threshold that would typically qualify you as being responsible for his upkeep for Child Benefit purposes

Do you have any plans to increase your contributions to at least match the Child Benefit rate (£25.60 per week or more)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I can't really afford to increase what I'm paying at the moment. The £10 a week is what I can manage right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information with me. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16, so age-eligible)
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with his mum (your ex-partner), not with you
- You contribute £10 per week towards his upkeep
- You cannot increase your contributions to match the Child Benefit rate

According to the Child Benefit rules, you would normally qualify if you're responsible for a child, which means either living with them OR paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (currently £25.60 per week for an eldest/only child) towards their upkeep.

Since Alex doesn't live with you and your contributions (£10/week) are below the Child Benefit threshold amount, you would not meet the criteria for being considered "responsible" for Alex under the Child Benefit rules.

Additionally, only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child. Since Alex lives with his mum, she would be the person who could claim Child Benefit for him if she's not already doing so.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Assessment Complete: You are INELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

I'm sorry, but based on your circumstances, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

The main reason is that to claim Child Benefit for a child who doesn't live with you, you need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment (£25.60 per week) towards their upkeep. Your current contribution of £10 per week, while helpful, falls below this threshold.

Since Alex lives with his mum, she would be the appropriate person to claim Child Benefit for him if she's not already doing so, as she is the one providing his day-to-day care.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about Child Benefit?
